message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches for abdominal aortic aneurysm with aligned trait_reported/trait_efo and diagnosis-style phenotyping_reported. PGS000753 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused AAA genetics study (Circulation; Million Veteran Program context) and reports a PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44), which is a PRS-comparable signal of discriminative strength when PRS-only AUC is not available. Competing candidates either appear to be framework/benchmarking-derived (e.g., PGS001784 from a global biobank portability paper; PGS002054 from a UKB portability study) or report only full-model discrimination metrics (e.g., PGS003973 C-index 0.882; PGS003429 AUROC 0.708; PGS003972 AUROC 0.69) that are not directly comparable to PRS-only performance and may be covariate-driven. The main limitation is that PGS000753 uses a sparse P+T model with only 29 variants and lacks PRS-only AUC/R2, while several newer PRS-CS/LDpred2 models are genome-wide and could plausibly perform better, but the context does not provide PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUC/OR/HR) to resolve this confidently."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002738","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All four candidates are direct matches to the target concept (alcohol dependence / alcohol use disorder), but the evidence is not strong enough for a high-confidence pick because none reports PRS-only AUROC or PRS-only R2, and covariates are unknown for the two AUD-labeled models. Among the set, PGS002738 has the strongest visible discriminative evidence via an OR(top 10% vs rest)=1.96 (95% CI 1.54–2.51) for alcohol use disorder with trait_efo explicitly 'alcohol dependence', and it is developed in a disease-focused multi-cohort context (MVP, UKB) with EUR evaluation (n=7,900). The main limitation is the lack of PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2) and unclear covariate adjustment, which prevents a clearly high-quality recommendation versus the alternative direct-match scores (PGS000201/PGS000202 with small ΔR2 values and PGS002739 evaluated only in African American samples)."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS004913","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo = alcoholic liver cirrhosis) with broadly aligned endpoints. PGS004913 is preferred because it is explicitly disease-focused on alcohol-associated cirrhosis among heavy drinkers, uses a standard PRS construction pipeline (PRSice-2), reports PRS-comparable variance explained (R²=0.029) and an OR (top vs bottom PRS deciles)=4.4, and uses only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), making the reported signal more interpretable as PRS contribution than full-model discrimination. PGS000704 reports only a full-model C-index (0.711) from a broad biomarker genetics paper and includes age/sex/PCs; without PGS-only metrics its apparent performance is hard to attribute to the PRS. PGS001777 is highly endpoint-aligned and shows strong stratification (OR top 20% vs bottom 20% = 6.18) but is extremely sparse (3 variants), has unknown covariates, and has a small validation sample (n=1,390), limiting confidence. Overall confidence is moderate (not high) because none of the candidates provides a clearly labeled PGS-only AUROC and the available metrics are not fully comparable across studies."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS005048","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris (EFO: angina pectoris) with endpoint-faithful phenotyping strings (e.g., ICD10 I20, PheCode 411.3, or angina diagnosis/self-report). Among models with comparable reported discrimination, the MVP PheCode-based set (PGS005047–PGS005059) provides consistent European validation C-index values around ~0.75–0.77; within that cluster, PGS005048 has the highest reported European full-model C-index (0.7669) and a strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.487, 95% CI 1.41–1.56), supporting meaningful PRS signal. Competing UKB pan-trait sparse snpnet models (PGS001260/PGS001261/PGS001262) report explicit PGS-only AUROC (~0.58) and small PGS-only R2 (~0.012), and their very high full-model AUROC values are likely largely covariate-driven; additionally, the domain guidance flags the 'across 813 traits' framework as less reliable for external performance. Key limitation: for the MVP models (including PGS005048), the reported C-index is a full-model metric (not explicitly PGS-only), and training details are listed as N/A, so PRS-only comparability is incomplete; several MVP siblings are very close in C-index/OR, leaving residual uncertainty in picking a single clear winner."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001267","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 9 candidates are direct matches to ankylosing spondylitis by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported. Among them, PGS001267 provides the most PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports both PGS-only AUROC (0.7265) and PGS-only R² (0.0988), plus full-model AUROC with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). Its PRS-only R² is also below the provided EUR liability-scale heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.399), passing the sanity-check. Competing UKB portability models (PGS001876, PGS002089) lack AUROC/R² and only report partial correlation, and the Taiwanese EAS models (PGS003420–PGS003424) report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates and small validation (n=1,298), making their metrics less comparable. Main limitation: PGS001267 comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (\"across 813 traits\"), which domain guidance flags as often less reliable for external generalization; additionally, PGS001268 is a very close sibling with slightly higher full-model AUROC/R² but uses a time-to-event endpoint, leaving some residual ambiguity."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS005252","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for aortic stenosis are present (PGS005252, PGS005254, PGS005255, PGS005256). PGS005252 is best supported in the provided metadata because it has the most endpoint-faithful phenotype description (incident aortic stenosis cases), reports a strong time-to-event discrimination metric (C-index 0.87) and a strong per-SD effect size (HR 1.92), and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDPred2) with a large variant set (~1.12M) in EUR development/evaluation. The main limitation is that the reported C-index is a full-model metric with many clinical covariates (e.g., diabetes, hypertension, CAD, hyperlipidemia, BMI, smoking, renal failure), and no PRS-only AUROC/R² or incremental metrics are shown, so the PRS-specific contribution cannot be cleanly compared against the other direct-match models; confidence is therefore moderate rather than high."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001135","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for the exact target trait exist (trait_efo=arthritis), notably PGS001135 (\"Arthritis (nos)\") and the Commun Biol \"M13 (Other arthritis)\" models (PGS004477, PGS004547). PGS001135 has the cleanest endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported=\"Arthritis (nos)\") and provides PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.53928; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.00291), which are interpretable and consistent with the provided heritability ceiling guidance (well below h2_liability=0.0610). In contrast, PGS004477/PGS004547 match the arthritis EFO but report only an OR without PRS-only discrimination metrics and have unknown covariates, limiting comparability. Overall, an exact-match model is available and reasonably supported, but confidence is limited because the PRS-only signal for generic arthritis is modest and many other arthritis-related models in the context target specific subtypes rather than the umbrella trait."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002727","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for asthma are abundant (66). Among the visible set, PGS002727 is the most strongly supported by a combination of endpoint alignment and PRS-relevant performance evidence: it targets pediatric asthma (still asthma; partial endpoint restriction), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; 985,837 variants), and reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.57, 95% CI 1.55–1.60) alongside full-model AUROC=0.66 and R²=0.04, with very large validation (n=391,820) and multi-ancestry evaluation. Competing models either come from pan-trait/framework families (e.g., UKB ‘813 traits’ snpnet scores) or lack comparable PRS-only metrics/effect sizes (many report only full-model AUROC or partial correlation), or have endpoint packaging/covariate concerns (e.g., family-history/environmental risk score covariates in PGS000799) or narrower endpoints (incident-only/time-to-event). Main limitation: PGS002727’s phenotype is explicitly pediatric asthma and covariates are listed as unknown, so despite strong effect-size evidence, it is not a clean generic asthma endpoint with fully transparent comparability; several adult/general-asthma candidates exist with reasonable metrics (e.g., PRS-CS-auto PGS001782 AUROC=0.659; snpnet doctor-diagnosed PGS001344 full-model AUROC=0.666) but their evidence is either more framework-like or less PRS-isolated, leaving residual uncertainty."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002755","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct EFO matches to atopic eczema, but several have endpoint mismatches: PGS003459/PGS003486/PGS004903 are evaluated on paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis (therapy-/context-specific rather than generic atopic eczema), and PGS001773 targets moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis in Canadian cohorts with a very high full-model AUROC (0.93) that is not PRS-comparable and may be covariate-driven per the provided domain guidance. Among the remaining incident atopic dermatitis candidates, PGS002755 (PRS-CS; genome-wide, 1,090,702 variants) has strong phenotype alignment (incident atopic dermatitis), clean/basic covariates, and reports an HR (high vs low PRS) of 1.249 (1.123–1.391) in a large European evaluation (n=337,910), providing the most directly interpretable PRS signal in this context. However, confidence is limited because no candidate reports PRS-only AUROC/R², and PGS004587 is also incident AD with similar evaluation size and an HR (1.153) but insufficient additional metadata here to clearly resolve which is superior beyond the modestly stronger HR and more polygenic method/variant count for PGS002755."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS005168","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Multiple direct-match atrial fibrillation PRS candidates are present. PGS005168 is best supported in the provided context because it is a disease-focused, multi-cohort atrial fibrillation PRS (Nat Genet 2025 meta-analysis; PRS-CS; 382,963 variants) with endpoint-aligned phenotyping_reported ('Atrial fibrillation') and basic-plus-clinical risk adjustment that includes CHARGE-AF but still reports strong discrimination (C-index 0.8718, European validation n=52,757) and strong per-SD effect size (HR 1.6663; beta 0.5106). Competing candidates either come from pan-trait/portability frameworks (e.g., UKB sparse/portability papers), are horizon-packaged 5-year risk models (PGS004612/PGS004613) which domain guidance flags as negative evidence for standalone PRS quality, have weaker/older evidence (e.g., PGS000016 R2=0.029), or are GWAS-hit small-SNP sets mainly used in interaction/exposure studies without PRS-comparable metrics. Confidence is not High because many candidates report only full-model metrics (limiting comparability), and PGS005168’s covariates include a named clinical risk calculator (CHARGE-AF), which domain guidance indicates can inflate full-model discrimination and reduces certainty about standalone PRS contribution in the absence of explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001263","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All four candidates are direct matches at the concept level (atrial flutter explicitly or via the combined AF/flutter endpoint). PGS001263 has the strongest endpoint fidelity to the target (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both 'Atrial flutter') and provides PRS-comparable metrics including PGS-only AUROC=0.617 and PGS-only R2=0.025, which is below the provided EUR heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0157; h2_liability=0.1443), supporting metric plausibility. However, confidence is limited because PGS001263 (and PGS001339) come from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework ('across 813 traits'), which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly, and the alternative portability-framework models (PGS001841/PGS002050) use stronger genome-wide shrinkage/penalized methods but lack PRS-only AUROC/R2 (only partial-r), making cross-candidate performance comparison incomplete. Given the need to prioritize phenotype alignment and comparable PRS-only metrics with the visible evidence, PGS001263 is the best-supported direct-match choice but remains sub-optimal due to framework-origin and incomplete comparability versus the other candidates."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000327","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Both candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo (autism spectrum disorder) and are EUR-evaluated. PGS000327 has stronger endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported is explicitly autism spectrum disorder) and comes from an ASD-focused Nat Genet study, with supportive PRS signal evidence including OR per SD 1.33 (moderate) and higher reported R² (0.0245) than the alternative. PGS002790 has a notable phenotype mismatch (phenotyping_reported: psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)) despite the ASD label, and shows weaker reported partial R² (~0.0055), making it less well-supported as an ASD diagnosis PRS. Confidence is not High because neither model reports clearly PRS-only discrimination metrics (e.g., PGS-only AUROC), and the R² fields appear to be full-model/partial metrics rather than explicitly PRS-only, limiting comparability."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000452","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All listed candidates are direct matches to basal cell carcinoma by trait_reported/trait_efo, but endpoint fidelity differs: most are generic “Basal cell carcinoma”, while PGS005207 is explicitly restricted to “risk of basal cell carcinoma in childhood cancer survivors” (a special-population/survivorship endpoint), making it less aligned to the generic target trait. Among the generic BCC models, the Cancer PRSweb family (PGS000445–PGS000459) provides multiple coherent, endpoint-faithful options with comparable basic covariates (age/sex/batch/PCs). Within that family, PGS000452 (GWAS Hits, 28 variants) has the strongest visible performance package: highest full-model AUROC among siblings (0.632, tied with PGS000454), the highest reported Nagelkerke pseudo-R² (0.0487), and a strong per-SD OR (1.663) plus strong top-1% vs rest OR (3.61). The main limitation is that none of the candidates report PRS-only AUROC/R², so comparisons rely on full-model metrics and effect sizes (which are not fully PRS-comparable), and PGS000454 is essentially tied on AUROC/R² with very similar covariates, leaving some residual uncertainty in choosing between near-clones."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002032","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches to the target concept via trait_efo including “bilirubin metabolism disease.” However, PGS000924 is from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse framework (“across 813 traits”) with a very small variant set (5) and time-to-event phenotyping, which domain guidance flags as a common underperforming archetype despite reporting high full-model/PGS-only AUROC and R2; additionally its reported PGS-only R2 (0.218) exceeds the provided local heritability ceiling estimate (h2_obs=0.0889), raising comparability/sanity-check concerns. The two remaining candidates (PGS001824 and PGS002032) have tighter endpoint fidelity (“Disorders of bilirubin excretion”) and come from the same portability study with identical reported partial-r (~0.0716) and similar covariates; between them, PGS002032 uses LDpred2 with a genome-wide variant set (19,768), which is structurally favored over a much sparser penalized regression score (22 variants) when other evidence is essentially tied. Confidence is only Moderate because neither portability model reports PRS-comparable AUROC/R2 beyond partial-r, and both are from a framework/portability context rather than a clearly disease-focused multi-cohort study."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002786","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches to the bipolar disorder spectrum (PGS002786: bipolar disorder; PGS002787: bipolar I; PGS002788: bipolar II) and share the same publication, method (SDPR), EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, and similar very large variant counts (~935k–949k), so there is no clearly superior study-design cluster signal to separate them. For the target trait labeled broadly as “bipolar disorder,” PGS002786 has the closest trait_reported/trait_efo alignment. However, endpoint fidelity is unclear/possibly mismatched across all three because phenotyping_reported fields describe non-diagnostic cognitive/behavioral measures (e.g., pattern comparison; Dsm5 depression; sluggish cognitive tempo) rather than a bipolar disorder case-control/diagnosis endpoint, and the only visible performance is very small partial R² values (~0.0025–0.0031) without PRS-only AUROC/AUC. Given this limited and potentially non-comparable endpoint/performance evidence, the best choice is only weakly supported, hence DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL with low confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002034","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches at the EFO level to the target concept (blood coagulation disease), but endpoint fidelity is imperfect across the set: PGS001033 uses a time-to-event phenotype (“TTE other coagulation defects”) and comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper (813 traits), which domain guidance flags as a systematic generalization risk despite having reported AUROC/R². PGS001826 and PGS002034 target a specific congenital coagulation-factor deficiency subtype (congenital vitamin K-dependent coagulation factors deficiency), which is narrower than the umbrella target but still within blood coagulation diseases; both come from the same UKB portability framework and report similar partial-r (~0.056) with no PRS-only AUROC/R². Between those two near-clones, PGS002034 is structurally preferred because it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with many more variants (32,552 vs 45) while keeping the same endpoint/covariates/publication context, making it the best-supported choice available here. Confidence is limited because the best candidate is a subtype rather than a clearly generic blood-coagulation-disease endpoint, and the pool is dominated by framework/portability studies with limited comparable PRS-only performance reporting."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS004153","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for breast carcinoma are abundant; among those shown, PGS004153 is a direct breast cancer model (trait_efo=breast carcinoma; phenotyping_reported=Breast cancer) with strong reported discrimination in European evaluation (AUROC 0.6625 with R² 0.0764) and strong effect size (OR 1.83 per SD), and it uses an explicitly clean covariate set (covariates=0), reducing concern that performance is driven by clinical risk-factor packaging. Competing direct-match models include other high-performing UKB-based method-benchmark scores (e.g., PGS004040/PGS004025 with AUROC ~0.6598, R² ~0.0736–0.0739) and earlier disease-focused scores (e.g., PGS000007 full_model_auc 0.78 but with age/sex covariates and without PRS-only metrics), but within the visible evidence PGS004153 has the strongest combined AUROC/R²/effect-size package while remaining endpoint-faithful. Main limitation: multiple near-tied high-performing direct-match candidates from the same 2023 benchmarking family exist with very similar endpoints and metrics, and the context does not provide external (non-UKB) validation comparisons to clearly separate them, so confidence is not high."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000316","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All listed candidates are direct matches to celiac disease by trait_efo, but they differ in endpoint fidelity and in whether reported metrics are PRS-comparable. PGS000316 has a clean, direct endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Coeliac disease), is not from a pan-trait/portability framework paper, and reports strong discrimination (full-model AUROC=0.879 with CI) with very large validation (n=379,767), making it the most broadly supported disease-focused option in the provided set. The main limitation is that the AUROC shown is a full-model metric (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R²), and covariates are listed as Unknown, so the PRS-only contribution and comparability cannot be confirmed from the context; meanwhile some alternatives either have only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates (e.g., PGS000040) or come from framework/portability studies (e.g., PGS001301, PGS001856/PGS002067) which domain guidance cautions against when disease-focused options exist."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003428","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo=cervical carcinoma; phenotyping_reported is cervical cancer/incident cervical cancer). PGS003428 is preferred because it comes from a cervical-phenotype GWAS meta-analysis study explicitly aimed at risk stratification, uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred) with a very large variant set (2,894,555), and reports a moderate per-SD effect size (HR=1.33) with European evaluation—together providing the strongest structural and disease-focused evidence among the pool. Main limitation: across candidates, reported discrimination is mostly full-model AUROC/C-index (not clearly PRS-only), and the C-index for PGS003428 (0.613) is not directly comparable to the higher full-model AUROC (~0.745) reported for PGS000073/PGS000784 due to differing covariate sets and lack of PRS-only metrics; therefore the selection is not high-confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS004546","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches to cholelithiasis (either exact cholelithiasis/K80 or the closely related composite “cholelithiasis and cholecystitis”). However, most candidates lack PRS-comparable discrimination metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²), making ranking uncertain. PGS004546 is preferred because it is endpoint-aligned (ICD10 K80 cholelithiasis), uses a multi-score aggregation method (RFDiseasemetaPRS; structurally favored in the provided domain knowledge), and reports a per-SD effect size (OR=1.2986) that is stronger than its sibling PGS004476 (OR=1.2194). The main limitation is that PGS004546 provides no AUROC/R² and has unknown covariates, while the only model with explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS001174) comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework that the domain knowledge flags as typically less reliable for external performance despite having reported PGS-only AUROC/R²."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002237","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Multiple direct-match CKD PRS candidates are present. PGS002237 is best supported overall because it is explicitly CKD-focused (Nat Med: “Genome-wide polygenic score to predict chronic kidney disease across ancestries”), uses a clinically specific CKD definition (stage 3+; eGFR <45 ml/min/1.73m2), has large development (UKB; n=279,819), multi-ancestry evaluation, and reports supportive discrimination/effect evidence (full-model AUROC 0.78 in European validation; OR 1.47). However, confidence is limited because the reported AUROC appears to be a full-model metric with substantial clinical covariates (hypertension, diabetes, BMI, medication use, etc.) and no PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided, making cross-model PRS-only comparability weak; several other direct-match candidates also lack PRS-only metrics, and some are endpoint-adjacent (e.g., eGFR-based or incident-only), so the selection cannot be upgraded to high-confidence based on the visible evidence alone."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001783","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match COPD candidates are present (PGS001332/PGS001333/PGS001334/PGS001783/PGS001788/PGS004466/PGS004536; plus chronic airway obstruction models mapped to COPD). Among these, PGS001783 is preferred because it is an exact COPD endpoint (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both COPD), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto) with a very large variant set (884,139), and comes from a broad multi-biobank development context rather than a sparse UKB-only pan-trait framework. It also reports a PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.038092), providing more directly interpretable PRS signal than candidates that report only full-model AUROC or only an OR without clear PRS-only discrimination. Main limitation: the evidence is still not decisive because several other direct COPD models exist with different reporting conventions (e.g., PGS001788 has much larger validation n but lower reported PRS R2; PGS004536 reports a stronger OR but lacks PRS-only AUC/R2 and has unknown covariates; the snpnet UKB framework models provide explicit PGS-only AUROC but are penalized by framework origin and show weak PRS-only metrics). This leaves residual uncertainty, so the direct-match recommendation is not high-confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS004621","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches to cirrhosis, but several are explicitly alcohol-related subtypes (PGS000704, PGS001777, PGS004913) and one has phenotype wording that appears alcohol-related despite a generic label (PGS000776), making them less clean for the broad target trait “cirrhosis of liver.” Among the generic cirrhosis candidates, PGS004621 has the strongest structural and study-support package visible here: it is explicitly for “Cirrhosis” (trait_efo: cirrhosis of liver; phenotyping_reported: Cirrhosis), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with a very large variant set (1,089,806), and is evaluated in Europeans with a very large validation sample (n=1,153,995). PGS000726 is also a clean direct match but is a sparse 12-variant GWS score with no AUROC/R2 reported (only ORs), leaving less direct evidence of broad polygenic capture. Confidence is Moderate (not High) because none of the candidates report clearly PRS-only discrimination metrics (the AUROCs shown are full-model), and endpoint/covariate comparability across studies cannot be fully verified from the provided metadata."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002034","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001826, PGS002034) and both align on the same EFO target and the same reported/phenotyped endpoint (“Congenital deficiency of other clotting factors (including factor VII)”), with similar ancestry context (UKB-derived portability study; DEV EUR, EVAL EUR/SAS) and identical basic covariates. Their reported PRS-comparable performance is essentially indistinguishable (partial-r 0.0562 vs 0.0563 with overlapping CIs), and neither reports AUC/R2 or effect sizes, limiting discrimination-based ranking. Given the tie on endpoint and metrics, method/structure becomes the main differentiator: PGS002034 uses LDpred2 with a much larger variant set (32,552 vs 45), which is a supportive structural signal for capturing polygenic signal when other evidence is equal. Overall quality remains sub-optimal because both models come from a UKB portability framework paper and lack standard PRS-only AUC/R2, so the best choice is only moderately supported."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS002042","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Both candidates are direct matches for the target trait (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all state corneal dystrophy) and come from the same UK Biobank portability publication with identical training cohort (UKB), training size (n=391,124), evaluation ancestry mix, covariates, and validation sample size (n=19,321), so endpoint fidelity and study context do not differentiate them. The main differentiators visible are (i) PRS-comparable performance: PGS002042 has a higher reported partial correlation (partial-r 0.0471 vs 0.0384 for PGS001835) in the selected European validation record, and (ii) structural properties: PGS002042 uses LDpred2 with many more variants (59,944 vs 38), which is generally supportive for polygenic signal capture when endpoints are otherwise identical. Confidence is Moderate because both models are from a portability/framework-style paper (a known limitation for external generalization) and neither reports standard PRS-only AUROC/R2 or effect sizes, leaving only partial-r as the comparable metric."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003725","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for coronary artery disease are abundant (85). Among the visible candidates, PGS003725 is a strong direct match on endpoint fidelity (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both explicitly coronary artery disease) and comes from a disease-focused, multi-ancestry CAD PRS study (Nat Med 2023; LDpred2; 1,296,172 variants) with supportive per-SD effect sizes (HR 1.75; OR 2.14) and large validation (n=308,264) across multiple ancestries, consistent with domain guidance favoring endpoint fidelity plus robust disease-focused study context and strong effect sizes when PRS-only metrics are not available. However, confidence is not High because many other direct CAD models are also endpoint-faithful and some report higher full-model AUROC (e.g., PGS001780 AUROC 0.913; PGS000018 AUROC 0.89), but these are full-model metrics with varying/unknown covariate packaging and are not PRS-only comparable; additionally, PGS003725 lacks explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2, limiting clean cross-model performance comparison."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001331","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches to Crohn disease (trait_efo=Crohn disease; phenotyping_reported indicates Crohn’s disease endpoints). PGS001331 is preferred over its near-clone sibling PGS001330 because it has slightly stronger PRS-comparable performance in the selected European validation (PGS-only AUROC 0.579 vs 0.576; PGS-only R2 0.00677 vs 0.00621; full-model AUROC 0.613 vs 0.603; incremental AUROC 0.027 vs 0.024) with essentially the same basic covariates and training context.
